decisions.reason: As a product line close to the core offer and already given its own webpage, it reflects visible commitment and sunk development effort, so management would be unlikely to withdraw it after only one year.

Although only mentioned briefly on the website, it fits the firm's announced push into automation and can plausibly be defended as still needing time for market adoption, which supports continued commitment.

This line is close to the established business and benefits from the firm's modular technology base, but its lower public visibility makes it somewhat easier to discontinue than the more prominently presented launches.
Because it is a core-adjacent product line with its own page, management has both reputational and resource-based reasons to persist with it despite any early uncertainty.
Its own webpage signals public commitment and it is close to the existing formwork offering, so escalation of commitment makes retention more likely than early withdrawal.

This product is still close to the core business, but as a less prominently presented single component it carries the weakest visible commitment and is therefore the most droppable of the group, though still more likely to be kept.
